words.definition: The leader of a country that has no king or queen.
words.example: The president gave a speech last night.

words.definition: A person who is in charge of a government department.
words.example: The health minister announced new rules today.

words.definition: A plan of action agreed by a government, company or group.
words.example: The company has a strict no-smoking policy.

words.definition: The group of people who make the laws of a country.
words.example: Parliament will vote on the bill next week.

words.definition: The person who is elected to lead a city or town.
words.example: The mayor opened the new library.

words.definition: A planned set of activities to achieve a goal, like winning an election.
words.example: Her campaign focuses on lower taxes.

words.definition: A public event where people show they disagree with something.
words.example: Thousands joined the protest downtown.

words.definition: A discussion in which people give different opinions.
words.example: There was a heated debate on TV last night.

words.definition: A change that makes a system or law better.
words.example: The government promised tax reform.

words.definition: A system in which people choose their leaders by voting.
words.example: Democracy depends on people voting.

words.definition: The system of money, trade and jobs in a country.
words.example: The economy is growing slowly.

words.definition: The production of goods, or a particular type of business.
words.example: He works in the tourism industry.

words.definition: The buying and selling of goods between people or countries.
words.example: Trade between the two countries has doubled.

words.definition: A product that is sold to another country.
words.example: Coffee is the country's main export.

words.definition: A product that is brought in from another country.
words.example: Imports of oil have fallen this year.

words.definition: The money you make when you sell something for more than it cost.
words.example: The shop made a small profit last month.

words.definition: To put money into something to make more money.
words.example: She invested her savings in a small business.

words.definition: A general rise in prices over time.
words.example: Inflation makes everything more expensive.

words.definition: The amount of something that is available.
words.example: There's a shortage in the supply of fresh fruit.

words.definition: The amount of something that people want to buy.
words.example: Demand for electric cars is rising.

words.definition: To study something carefully to understand it.
words.example: We need to analyze the data first.

words.definition: To find an answer using numbers.
words.example: Can you calculate the total cost?

words.definition: To say what will happen in the future.
words.example: No one can predict the weather perfectly.

words.definition: To look at something carefully.
words.example: The doctor examined my knee.

words.definition: To show that something is true.
words.example: Can you prove it?

words.definition: To guess an amount or value.
words.example: I estimate it will take two hours.

words.definition: To find out or decide something.
words.example: We need to determine the cause of the problem.

words.definition: To judge the quality or size of something.
words.example: The teacher assesses each student's progress.

words.definition: To decide something after thinking about the facts.
words.example: We concluded that the plan wouldn't work.

words.definition: To work something out. Often used in "figure out".
words.example: I can't figure out how this works.

words.definition: A feeling of liking and caring about someone.
words.example: She shows her affection with small gestures.

words.definition: Staying faithful and supportive to someone or something.
words.example: I admire his loyalty to his friends.

words.definition: Hurting someone who trusted you.
words.example: Lying to her felt like a betrayal.

words.definition: A promise or a strong dedication to something.
words.example: A marriage needs commitment from both people.

words.definition: A feeling of admiration for someone's qualities.
words.example: I have a lot of respect for my teachers.

words.definition: To draw people toward something or make them interested.
words.example: The festival attracts thousands of visitors.

words.definition: A strong connection between people.
words.example: The two sisters share a close bond.

words.definition: A feeling of sorrow for someone else's trouble.
words.example: I have a lot of sympathy for her. It's been a hard year.

words.definition: The ability to understand and share how someone else feels.
words.example: A good friend shows empathy.

words.definition: To respect and like someone or something very much.
words.example: I really admire how hard she works.

words.definition: The crime of stealing.
words.example: Car theft is rising in this area.

words.definition: The crime of taking things from a person or place by force.
words.example: There was a robbery at the bank.

words.definition: A thief who breaks into buildings.
words.example: A burglar broke into our house last night.

words.definition: A person who might have committed a crime.
words.example: The police have arrested a suspect.

words.definition: To take someone to the police because they may have committed a crime.
words.example: They arrested him on Friday night.

words.definition: To take something that does not belong to you.
words.example: Someone stole my bike.

words.definition: The crime of tricking someone to get money.
words.example: He was jailed for credit card fraud.

words.definition: To try to find out the facts about something.
words.example: Police are investigating the accident.

words.definition: Protection of people and places from danger or crime.
words.example: Security is tight at the airport.

words.definition: To walk or drive around an area to check it is safe.
words.example: Police patrol the streets at night.

words.definition: Careless about danger or consequences.
words.example: It was reckless to drive in that storm.

words.definition: Not paying enough attention.
words.example: A careless mistake cost us the game.

words.definition: Moving in an awkward way and often breaking things.
words.example: I'm so clumsy. I dropped my plate again.

words.definition: Shy and easily frightened.
words.example: The puppy is timid around strangers.

words.definition: Not willing to spend or give money.
words.example: He's too stingy to leave a tip.

words.definition: Clever and funny.
words.example: She's witty and always has a good comeback.

words.definition: Easily tricked because you believe everything.
words.example: Don't be so gullible. It's obviously a scam.

words.definition: Not willing to do something.
words.example: He was reluctant to ask for help.

words.definition: Continuing to try even when it is difficult.
words.example: She's persistent. She called every day until they answered.

words.definition: Careful not to upset people by what you say.
words.example: That wasn't very tactful of you.

words.definition: A place where people get medical care without staying overnight.
words.example: I went to a walk-in clinic for my cough.

words.definition: A doctor who knows a lot about one area of medicine.
words.example: My doctor referred me to a specialist.

words.definition: The doctor's decision about what illness a person has.
words.example: The diagnosis was a relief. It wasn't serious.

words.definition: Medical care to make a sick person better.
words.example: She is receiving treatment for a back problem.

words.definition: A medicine that protects you from a disease.
words.example: Have you had the flu vaccine this year?

words.definition: A disease that spreads quickly among many people.
words.example: The epidemic spread across the region.

words.definition: A doctor who performs operations.
words.example: The surgeon explained the procedure.

words.definition: Protected against a disease.
words.example: You become immune after you've had the illness.

words.definition: A general medical examination.
words.example: I have my yearly checkup tomorrow.

words.definition: A room in a hospital with beds for patients.
words.example: She's recovering in the maternity ward.

words.definition: Exact and accurate.
words.example: I need precise measurements.

words.definition: Able to change easily.
words.example: My schedule is flexible.

words.definition: Fair and sensible.
words.example: That's a reasonable price.

words.definition: Showing good judgment.
words.example: It's sensible to save money.

words.definition: Useful and realistic.
words.example: Those shoes aren't very practical.

words.definition: Connected to the subject being discussed.
words.example: That comment isn't relevant.

words.definition: Right for a particular purpose.
words.example: Is this movie suitable for children?

words.definition: Enough, or good enough.
words.example: The food was adequate, but nothing special.

words.definition: Absolutely necessary.
words.example: Water is essential for life.

words.definition: The best possible.
words.example: This apartment is ideal for a small family.

words.definition: An arrangement to keep a room, seat or ticket for you.
words.example: I made a booking for two nights.

words.definition: A set of rooms in a hotel.
words.example: They upgraded us to a suite.

words.definition: The work of cleaning rooms in a hotel.
words.example: Housekeeping comes every morning.

words.definition: Useful features that make a place comfortable.
words.example: The hotel has great amenities, like a pool and gym.

words.definition: The time when you leave a hotel, or the place in a shop where you pay.
words.example: Checkout is at eleven.

words.definition: Given free of charge.
words.example: We got complimentary breakfast.

words.definition: Of very high quality.
words.example: We booked a deluxe room.

words.definition: A hotel worker who helps guests with requests.
words.example: Ask the concierge for restaurant tips.

words.definition: A small fridge with drinks in a hotel room.
words.example: The minibar is expensive.

words.definition: Sheets and towels, or cloth made from a plant called flax.
words.example: Fresh linen is provided every day.

words.definition: To give money or things to help others.
words.example: We donated our old clothes to charity.

words.definition: To act dishonestly to win something.
words.example: He cheated on the exam.

words.definition: To say something rude to someone.
words.example: I didn't mean to insult you.

words.definition: To frighten someone so they do what you want.
words.example: He tried to intimidate the witness.

words.definition: To speak angrily to someone about something they did wrong.
words.example: Mom scolded me for coming home late.

words.definition: To ask for God's protection. People also say "bless you" after a sneeze.
words.example: Bless you!

words.definition: To laugh at someone in an unkind way.
words.example: Don't mock him. He's trying his best.

words.definition: To use strength or power to frighten or hurt a weaker person.
words.example: He bullied other kids at school.

words.definition: To say that something must not be done.
words.example: The rules forbid phones in class.

words.definition: To forgive someone or excuse a mistake.
words.example: Pardon me. I didn't catch that.
